audit_items.proof_trace: The cache key omits KzgCommitments from its construction, using only KzgCommitmentsInclusionProof and SignedBlockHeader hash. Two data columns with identical proofs and headers but different KzgCommitments will share a cache entry, causing the second to bypass verification incorrectly.
audit_items.attack_scenario: Attacker sends valid data column A, which gets verified and cached. Then sends malicious data column B with same proof/header but altered KzgCommitments. B skips verification via cache hit and is accepted despite invalid commitments.
